input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 binds Customer to Vendor as its sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term. This is exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit — walk-away territory under the rule, and it fails the fallback (which requires a defined category, a 12-month limit, and automatic termination on Vendor's service-level or delivery failure). It also directly conflicts with Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deletion of Section 2.2 is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position and resolves the internal inconsistency. No other exclusivity provision binds Customer; the remaining "exclusive" references (licence grant, remedies, jurisdiction) are unrelated.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment in Section 2.2: our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on Customer, and this clause also contradicts Sections 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment). If Vendor needs some volume protection, we could consider exclusivity limited to a defined product category for no more than 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels or delivery dates.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 2.2 exclusivity obligation binding Customer
